title: Kamloops Home Energy Rebates 2026: Heat Pumps and Insulation for Older Homes
desc: Kamloops rebates for 2026 from BC Hydro, FortisBC and CleanBC, with Census numbers on a city where half of households live in homes built before 1981.
lead: Half of Kamloops households (51% of 39,915) live in a home built before 1981, and winters reach -34.3°C. That combination makes insulation the rebate to look at before anything else.
cards_heading: What you can claim in Kamloops in 2026
cards_intro: Amounts come from the program pages we re-read on October 2, 2026. Each card is a maximum, and most depend on how your home is heated.

cards.title: Whole-home heat pump
cards.note: Must replace electric heat such as baseboards or an electric furnace, meet 100% of the heating load at -5C and be installed by a Home Performance Contractor Network member.

cards.title: Partial heat pump
cards.note: For a heat pump that covers at least half of the heating load while replacing electric heat.

cards.title: Limited-time bonus
cards.note: Extra money on heat pump installs completed between August 1 and October 31, 2026.

cards.title: Income-qualified switch from gas, oil or propane
cards.note: CleanBC pays by income level (Level 3 / Level 2 / Level 1) for a central or three-head heat pump, for invoices from July 6, 2026.

cards.title: Insulation
cards.note: Attic, wall and basement or crawlspace work, paid per R-value added per square foot. Homes heated mainly by electricity only.

cards.title: Windows and doors
cards.note: $100 per opening, with a U-factor of 1.22 or lower.

cards.title: Heat pump water heater
cards.note: Only when it replaces an electric water heater.

cards.title: Solar panels
cards.note: $1,000 per kW, capped at half the cost, from an HPCN member installer.

cards.title: Battery storage
cards.note: Up to $1,500 on its own with solar, or up to $5,000 with Peak Saver enrolment.

cards.title: EV charger
cards.note: 50% of a new wall-mounted Level 2 charger, plus $200 for a power-management device.

sections: The 2021 Census counted 9,895 owner-occupied detached houses built before 1981 in Kamloops, with 70% of households owning overall and 50% living in detached houses. About 5.1% reported needing major repairs. These houses are the target for BC Hydro's insulation rebate of up to $5,500 and its window rebate of up to $2,000, both for homes heated mainly by electricity.

The January average low in our climate file is -6.1°C and the coldest day in 2015 to 2024 was -34.3°C. BC Hydro's heat pump rule asks the system to cover 100% of the heating load at -5°C, which is a much easier test on the coast than here, so ask an installer what the model delivers at -20°C and whether a backup is needed. Solar gets about 3.64 peak sun hours a day, a good number in this group.

Kamloops electricity is BC Hydro. A house on baseboards can claim up to $4,000 for a whole-home heat pump. A house heated by natural gas from FortisBC cannot claim the BC Hydro heat pump rebate, and an income-qualified household can instead use CleanBC at $3,500, $7,000 or $13,000. Above those income limits, insulation is the sound first step because it pays off whatever you burn.
Insulate first, then size the heat pump. A tighter house needs less equipment, and the heat pump load calculation should use the post-insulation numbers if the work will be done within a year.
installers_intro: These are the best-reviewed heat pump and heating companies in Kamloops on Google, weighted by review count. Nobody pays to be listed or to rank higher.
claim_steps: Measure the attic and ask for an insulation quote that lists R-value added.
Ask a heat pump installer what the model does at -20C.
Check CleanBC if income is lower.
faq: How cold is Kamloops compared with Kelowna?
The record low in 2015 to 2024 was -34.3 degrees Celsius against -24.0 degrees in Kelowna.
How many older homes are there?
9,895 owner-occupied detached houses were built before 1981.
Should I insulate before a heat pump?
Usually yes, because a tighter home needs a smaller system.
